overall: The AG found the Committee's notice topic "Approval of Expenditure of Funds" insufficiently specific, violating the OML, and ordered a re-noticed re-vote within 14 days or nullification of the March 27 approval.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the March 27 meeting notice topic 'Approval of Expenditure of Funds' was not sufficiently detailed to inform the public.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee acknowledges, and we find, that the topic was insufficiently specific.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that public comment was allowed only at the start of the meeting, so the vague notice deprived the public of a chance to speak against the expenditure.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that public bodies allow an opportunity for public comment during meetings in the first place , and therefore we do not separately review whether the insufficient meeting notice deprived the complainant and others of the opportunity to speak in opposition to the approval of expenditure of funds.

remedy: Post adequate notice and again discuss and vote on the approval of expenditure of funds for legal counsel within 14 days of the determination.
If no proper re-vote occurs within 14 days, nullify the approval voted at the March 27 meeting under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c)(3).
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
remedy_passage: If the Committee fails to vote to approve the expenditure at a properly noticed meeting within 14 days, the approval that was voted at its March 27 meeting shall be nullified, pursuant to G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c)(3).
